current_draft.content_markdown:
The Digital Government Authority (DGA) announced during LEAP 2026 in Riyadh that Saudi Arabia's Digital Experience Maturity Index has reached an "Advanced" level, securing a score of 87.06%. This significant milestone reflects the Kingdom's accelerated digital transformation efforts and its commitment to enhancing digital government services across the nation. The announcement, delivered by DGA Governor Eng. Ahmed bin Mohammed Alsuwaiyan, highlights a measurable progression in how citizens and residents interact with public platforms. The comprehensive assessment for the 2026 index evaluated 59 digital platforms, an increase from the 50 platforms assessed in 2025, demonstrating an expanding scope of digital governance and service delivery in the region. The results emphasize the strategic focus on user-centric design and the continuous refinement of digital interfaces to meet the evolving needs of the population. By establishing rigorous benchmarks, the DGA aims to ensure that public services remain responsive, efficient, and accessible to all demographics.

The evaluation process for the Saudi Arabia digital experience was rooted in four primary perspectives designed to measure effectiveness and user satisfaction comprehensively. These pillars included beneficiary satisfaction, user experience, complaints handling, and the underlying technologies and tools driving the platforms. The rigorous methodology ensures that the maturity index reflects not just technological adoption but the actual quality of service experienced by end-users. A remarkable aspect of the 2026 assessment was the sheer volume of public participation. Over 805,500 individuals took part in the "Evaluate Your Digital Experience" survey, representing a substantial increase from the 374,000 participants recorded the previous year. This surge in engagement underscores a growing public interest and reliance on digital channels for government interactions. It also provides the DGA with a vast dataset to identify pain points and areas requiring immediate attention, fostering a culture of continuous improvement within the public sector. The expanded scope of the survey allows for a more granular understanding of user behavior and preferences, enabling targeted interventions to enhance the overall digital ecosystem.

## Leading Platforms and Digital Inclusion

Among the 59 platforms evaluated, the [Absher platform](https://dga.gov.sa/en/news/results-digital-experience-maturity-index-2026) emerged as the top performer, achieving an impressive score of 94.38%. This high ranking reflects Absher's critical role and widespread adoption in facilitating essential government services for citizens and expatriates alike. Closely following was [Etimad](https://saudigazette.com.sa/article/663669), which secured the second position with a score of 94.36%. The strong performance of these platforms indicates a high level of reliability and user satisfaction in key administrative and financial service areas. Other notable platforms that demonstrated robust maturity included Senaei, Balady, and Tawakkalna, further illustrating the depth of the Kingdom's digital infrastructure. The consistent high performance of these core platforms demonstrates the effectiveness of sustained investment in digital capabilities and user experience optimization. By prioritizing seamless interactions and intuitive navigation, these platforms have set a high standard for digital service delivery in the region.

A crucial component of the maturity index is the Digital Inclusion sub-index, which measures the accessibility of digital services for all segments of society. In the 2026 assessment, this sub-index achieved a score of 76.98%, placing it at the "Empowered" level. This achievement reflects targeted efforts by the DGA and other government bodies to design services that accommodate persons with disabilities, the elderly, and other vulnerable groups. Ensuring digital inclusion is a fundamental aspect of the broader digital transformation strategy, aiming to leave no citizen behind as services increasingly migrate online. The focus on accessibility aligns with global best practices and highlights a commitment to equitable service delivery. By implementing inclusive design principles and conducting rigorous accessibility testing, the government aims to bridge the digital divide and ensure that all individuals can fully participate in the digital economy. This proactive approach to digital inclusion not only enhances the user experience for marginalized groups but also strengthens the overall resilience and inclusivity of the digital infrastructure.

## Strategic Context and Future Outlook

The rise in the Digital Experience Maturity Index 2026 is deeply intertwined with the objectives of [Saudi Vision 2030](https://www.alarabiya.net/aswaq/economy/2026/08/12/%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B3%D8%B9%D9%88%D8%AF%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%AA%D8%B1%D9%81%D8%B9-%D9%85%D8%A4%D8%B4%D8%B1-%D9%86%D8%B6%D8%AC-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%AA%D8%AC%D8%B1%D8%A8%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D8%B1%D9%82%D9%85%D9%8A%D8%A9-%D8%A7%D9%84%D9%89-8706-%D9%81%D9%8A-2026). The strategic framework emphasizes the development of a vibrant society and an ambitious nation, with digital transformation serving as a key enabler. By continuously improving the digital experience, Saudi Arabia is not only streamlining government operations but also fostering a more business-friendly environment and improving the overall quality of life for its residents. The progress reported at LEAP 2026 solidifies the Kingdom's global position in digital government, showcasing a proactive approach to adopting emerging technologies and refining service delivery models. The integration of advanced analytics, artificial intelligence, and cloud computing into public sector operations has been instrumental in driving these improvements, enabling more personalized and efficient service delivery. The ongoing commitment to digital excellence is expected to attract further investment and innovation, reinforcing the Kingdom's status as a leading digital economy in the region.

While the 87.06% score represents a significant achievement, the expanding scope of the assessment suggests that continuous improvement remains a priority. As more platforms are integrated into the evaluation process and user expectations evolve, maintaining and exceeding current maturity levels will require ongoing investment in technology and user-centric design. The DGA's commitment to expanding the evaluation criteria and increasing public participation in future surveys will be critical in identifying areas for further enhancement. The current trajectory indicates a strong foundation, but the dynamic nature of digital services necessitates a sustained focus on innovation and responsiveness to user feedback. Addressing emerging challenges, such as cybersecurity threats and data privacy concerns, will also be essential in maintaining public trust and ensuring the long-term success of the digital transformation agenda. By fostering collaboration between government agencies, private sector partners, and the public, the DGA aims to build a resilient and adaptable digital ecosystem that can meet the evolving needs of the Kingdom.
